questions.question: Which phase of virtual reality history is the period before the advent of digital computers?
options: The current growth phase
The formative years
The modern phase
The early era
questions.explanation: The early era is described as existing before the advent of digital computers.

questions.question: Which phase of virtual reality history runs from 1991 to 2015?
options: The modern phase
The early era
The formative years
The current growth phase
questions.explanation: The modern phase is given as running from 1991 to 2015.

questions.question: Why can a virtual reality headset create immersion from a flat display?
options: The headset adds smell and wind feedback
Stereoscopic vision lets the user perceive 2D images as 3D objects and space.
Head tracking makes the display generate true 3D light fields
Multiple sensors make the user feel motion
questions.explanation: VR headsets or display devices present 2D images, but stereoscopic vision makes the user perceive them as 3D objects and space, which is immersion.

questions.question: What is historically important about the pre-computer early era of virtual reality?
options: It proved that digital computers had already made practical VR possible
It showed that head-mounted displays were the defining feature of the era
It contained key developments that were conceptually similar to immersive VR experiences.
It already included complete immersive virtual environments
questions.explanation: The early era was before modern digital computers, but a few key developments were conceptually similar to immersive virtual reality experiences.

questions.question: How did an early compact stereoscope advance earlier stereoscopic devices?
options: It used multiple sensors to simulate motion
It created the illusion of depth in viewed images in a compact display.
It added head tracking with computer-generated images
It introduced smell, wind, and vibration feedback
questions.explanation: The compact-sized stereoscope was an early stereoscopic display that created a depth illusion and was an advancement over earlier stereoscopic devices.

questions.question: Why is the early flight simulator concept significant for immersive virtual reality?
options: It first demonstrated that 2D images can be perceived as 3D
It popularized the term virtual reality
It introduced the compact stereoscope
It evolved into simulators with multiple sensors that provide an immersive experience.
questions.explanation: The early flight simulator concept evolved into sophisticated simulators with multiple sensors, making it a precursor to modern multi-sensory immersive VR.

questions.question: Which pair of developments marks the beginning and end of the formative phase of virtual reality?
options: Development of head-mounted displays in the 1950s and popularization of the term virtual reality in the late 1980s
The appearance of computers in the 1940s and WTK software in 1992
Stereoscopic demonstrations in the 1830s and the CAVE system in 1992
Flight simulators in the 1920s and Oculus Rift in 2012
questions.explanation: The formative phase began with head-mounted display development in the 1950s and ended when the term virtual reality became popular in the late 1980s.

questions.question: What made Sensorama count as an immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition?
options: It combined force feedback with manipulation of on-screen objects
It combined commercial availability with a stereoscopic wide field of view
It combined head tracking with computer-generated imagery
It combined visual effects with stereo sound, smell, wind, and haptic vibrations
questions.explanation: Sensorama was considered the first immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition and stimulated multiple senses, including visual, auditory, smell, wind, and vibration effects.

questions.question: What capability made Sutherland's Sword of Damocles a milestone in head-mounted displays?
options: It provided force feedback while users manipulated objects on a screen
It demonstrated head tracking combined with computer-generated imagery
It provided pre-recorded smell, wind, and vibrations
It provided commercial availability with a stereoscopic wide field of view
questions.explanation: Sutherland's Sword of Damocles was the first HMD to demonstrate head tracking and computer-generated imagery together.

questions.question: What made NASA's VIVED a notable early head-tracked display?
options: It was the first immersive system to use smell, wind, and vibrations
It was a force-feedback device for feeling objects on a screen
It was a visually coupled system intended for pilot training
It was a commercially viable stereoscopic head-tracked HMD with a wide field of view
questions.explanation: VIVED was notable because it was the first commercially viable and available stereoscopic head-tracked HMD with a wide field of view.

questions.question: What term was proposed in the late 1980s and became the standard name for immersive technologies?
options: Immersive display
Virtual reality
Artificial reality
Virtual environment
questions.explanation: In the late 1980s, Jaron Lanier proposed the term virtual reality, and that term became the one used to refer to immersive technologies.

questions.question: How did head-mounted displays evolve over the historical development of virtual reality?
options: They were replaced by data gloves and haptic devices
They remained bulky but added smell and wind
They became more portable, less bulky, and more usable
They became less portable, more bulky, and less usable
questions.explanation: HMDs evolved from bulky late-1950s models through later HMDs into a more portable, less bulky, and more usable form.

questions.question: What effect did inexpensive virtual reality headsets such as the Oculus Rift have on virtual reality?
options: They made VR more affordable and greatly spurred interest
They limited VR to research laboratories
They made VR less affordable and reduced interest
They shifted VR development toward CAVE systems
questions.explanation: Facebook's purchase of the Oculus Rift headset tried to popularize it and make VR affordable for the masses. The availability of inexpensive headsets greatly spurred interest in VR.

questions.question: How does Sir Charles Wheatstone's stereoscopic demonstration connect to the way a VR headset creates immersion?
questions.reference_answer: Sir Charles Wheatstone's 1838 stereoscopic device established that the human brain can process two-dimensional images as three-dimensional objects. In VR, headsets present two-dimensional images, but stereoscopic vision makes the user perceive them as three-dimensional objects and space, and that perception is immersion.

questions.question: Why can Sensorama be treated as the first immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition of virtual reality?
questions.reference_answer: Morton Heilig introduced Sensorama in 1962, and it can be considered the first immersive virtual reality system under the modern definition of virtual reality. It was publicized as having 3D, wide vision, motion, color, stereo sound, smell, wind, and vibrations, and it stimulated all sensory organs. An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real because the person cannot distinguish the environment from the real environment, so multi-sensory stimulation like Sensorama's fits that definition.

questions.question: How did the availability of inexpensive headsets such as the Oculus Rift help VR move from the end of its modern phase into its current growth phase?
questions.reference_answer: The Oculus Rift was an inexpensive VR headset created by Palmer Luckey in 2012, and Facebook's purchase of it in 2014 helped try to popularize the headset and make VR affordable. The availability of inexpensive headsets such as the Oculus Rift greatly spurred interest in VR towards the end of its modern phase. The growth phase then began roughly in 2016, when many well-known companies released commercial VR headsets that made immersive experiences affordable to a large population.

questions.question: How do the 2016 commercial headset releases and the 2021 popularization of the metaverse connect within the current growth phase?
questions.reference_answer: The current growth phase began roughly in 2016 when many well-known companies released commercial virtual reality headsets, making immersive experiences affordable to a large population and spurring growth in the field. The metaverse term had been in use for more than 30 years and had existed in the research community since the 1990s, but in 2021 Zuckerberg of Meta popularized it. After that, people began taking an interest in the metaverse and interpreting it in different ways, which spurred further activity.
